articles.title: Nepal, Western Terai | Flood - Simplified Early Action Protocol Operations Update (sEAP No: sEAP2026NP03) - July 2026
articles.description: Country: Nepal Source: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies Please refer to the attached file. Flood is one of the most severe hazards in Nepal in terms of physical and socioeconomic losses. Major perennial rivers such as Koshi, Karnali, and Narayani often cause flooding across multiple districts of the Southern Terai, while rivers originating in the Mahabharat range, including West Rapti and Babai, frequently generate flash floods that disproportionately impact low-lying floodplains. The Terai’s vulnerable topography and dependence on agriculture further exacerbate flood impacts. Historically, floods have caused significant devastation. In 2017, prolonged rainfall from 11–14 August affected 31 districts, impacting an estimated 450,000 people and resulting in 43 deaths. According to the Government of Nepal’s National Planning Commission Post Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA) 2017, 41,626 houses were destroyed and 150,510 damaged, over 126,000 hectares of paddy were lost, and livestock—including 812,000 poultry and 9,400 cattle—suffered severe losses. Major flood disasters in 2006, 2008, 2013, 2014, and 2017 repeatedly affected Bardiya, Kailali, and Banke districts, causing widespread infrastructure damage, including roads, bridges, culverts, local markets, and residential areas. Flooding has also occurred outside the monsoon season, such as the October 2022 Babai flood affecting Bardiya district. Nepal Red Cross Society (NRCS) household surveys conducted in 2021–2022 show that along the Babai River, 25,247 families live in Barbardiya, Thakurbaba, Madhuwan, and Gulariya municipalities, while 21,032 families reside along the West Rapti River in Rapti Sonari, Duduwa, and Narainapur municipalities. Flooding in these districts has intensified between 2023 and 2025. In Banke district, particularly Rapti Sonari, Duduwa, and Narainapur, approximately 4,500–5,000 households were affected in 2023, rising to approx. 7,500 households in 2024, with nearly 1,500 displaced, and remaining high at 6,000 households in 2025. Impacts included repeated paddy crop losses, damage to irrigation systems and roads, and riverbank erosion. In Bardiya district, including Rajapur, Geruwa, Barbardiya, Thakurbaba, and Gulariya municipalities, approx. 7,000 households were affected in 2023, rising sharply to around 13,000 households in 2024—including approximately 3,000 displaced households—and 11,000 households affected in 2025. Damage encompassed inundation, extensive crop losses, livestock mortality, and infrastructure damage, alongside urban flooding in low-lying areas. These trends highlight the increasing severity and frequency of flood impacts in the West Rapti and Babai basins, underlining the continued support of anticipatory action, early warning systems, and community resilience measures.

articles.description: The end-Triassic mass extinction, 201 million years ago, is linked to volcanism that resulted from the break-up of Pangea and which pumped out vast amounts of CO2 into the atmosphere, causing extreme global warming of 5 to 10 degrees Celsius. articles.title: Horoscope for Tuesday, July 21, 2026
articles.description:
Moon alert

Avoid shopping (except food and gas) and important decisions from 5:30 to 9 a.m. Chicago time. After that, the moon moves from Libra into Scorpio.

Aries (March 21-April 19)

A positive day

Financial speculation might be rewarding today. Meanwhile, expect surprise invitations to socialize. You might also suddenly decide about a vacation or a future sports event. Relations with kids will be spontaneous and fun.

Taurus (April 20-May 20)

An average day

Avoid power struggles with partners, spouses and close friends today. Nevertheless, something special or favorable or financially attractive might benefit your family today. You might buy something for your home or receive a gift — or your family might have a new addition.

Gemini (May 21-June 20)

A positive day

Spontaneous short trips and opportunities to meet new faces and see new places will please you today. Meanwhile, work-related discussions might be challenging. Steer clear of controversial subjects like politics and religion because they could turn nasty. Stay calm.

Cancer (June 21-July 22)

A positive day

This is a financially fortuitous day for you. You might suddenly make more money or get a bit richer for some reason. If you have a chance to pursue a new job offer or ask for a raise, do it. Meanwhile, be patient with your kids and romantic partners to avoid arguments.

Leo (July 23-Aug. 22)

A positive day

An encounter with a friend or a member of a group might surprise you today because it turns out to be something other than what you expected. It might broaden your horizons in some way or increase your connections. Perhaps you will meet a new friend. Meanwhile, be patient at home.

Virgo (Aug. 23-Sept. 22)

An average day

Avoid arguments with daily contacts, siblings and relatives, especially if you are trying hard to make a point or convince others to agree with you. Give it up. Instead, focus on some inner realizations that might occur today — perhaps an epiphany? Listen to your inner world.

Libra (Sept. 23-Oct. 22)

A positive day

A friendship might delight you today. Or perhaps you'll become involved with an organization or club in a new way. Whatever happens will be unexpected and sudden. Meanwhile, avoid disagreements about money and possessions. Be smart.

Scorpio (Oct. 23-Nov. 21)

An average day

Today you might give in to impulsive or compulsive behavior. You might also encounter an emotional power struggle with someone — perhaps because someone is reacting to something that makes you suddenly look good? Something unexpected favors you! This might be jealousy.

Sagittarius (Nov. 22-Dec. 21)

A positive day

Unexpected opportunities to travel might fall into your lap today. If so, act quickly — this window of opportunity will be brief. Likewise, a chance to explore something in publishing, medicine, the law or higher education might also appear out of nowhere. Act fast.

Capricorn (Dec. 22-Jan. 19)

An average day

Avoid money squabbles today or arguments about possessions. Instead, keep your eyes open because you might benefit in practical ways or financial ways through the wealth and resources of someone else. Or you might get money back from the government. Could be anything. Ka-ching!

Aquarius (Jan. 20-Feb. 18)

An average day

You're high-viz today, which is why it's in your best interest not to have a public argument somewhere. Why end up with egg on your face? Instead, focus on partnerships and close relationships because something unexpected will delight you. Be open to whatever happens.

Pisces (Feb. 19-March 20)

An average day

Steer clear of controversial subjects today because they could become emotionally charged. Meanwhile, this is a great day to suddenly improve your health or your job. Your chance to do so will have a very short window, so if something arises be prepared to act fast. Something that is pet-related might also delight you.

If today is your birthday

Actor and comedian Robin Williams (1951-2014) shares your birthday. You are both extroverted and introverted. You're curious, determined and independent-thinking. You have an extraordinary understanding of human nature. This is a slower-paced year. It's OK to rest and rejuvenate your energy. Focus on relationships with those who are kind, helpful and supportive.

articles.title: Country diary: I’m immersed in the rich, chromatic aura of a summer meadow | Mark Cocker
articles.description: Hartington Meadows, Derbyshire: Amid a complex reticulation of stalks, stems, blooms and leaves, the right response might be to drop down before it In his glorious poem Haymaking , about a flower meadow, Edward Thomas describes how the fiery day “had a kernel sweet of cold” and “the white empty road was lightly strewn/With leaves”. The heat here, however, was unrelieved, and if the road was empty, it was also liquefying at its margin. Sweat banded my cap and ran in the creases at the backs of my bare legs, where, I noticed, the horseflies focused their attentions. Flower meadows, more than any other British land form, seem to be the most entangled and entangling places we have. They encircle and almost invade you with a sense of richness: not just the entwining hum of insect wings, nor the penetrating chromatic songs of the flowers themselves, but in an exuberant aura of living abundance.
